body: {"status":"ok","message-type":"work-list","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"facets":{},"total-results":1843861,"items":[{"abstract":"<jats:p>Language models are routinely given long, multispan inputs assembled from documents, chat history, tool outputs, and memory entries. When the model generates a response, it may draw on spans that are irrelevant to the query and produce a confident, coherent answer grounded in the wrong part of the context. This paper argues that such failures constitute a distinct phenomenon, which we call Ghost Context, and that the existing taxonomy of hallucination does not adequately capture them. A hallucinating model invents information that is absent from context. A model exhibiting Ghost Context uses information that is present but should not influence the current output. The error is not fabrication; it is misattribution. Critically, Ghost Context can occur even when every span in the context is individually authorized for the user and permissible for the application, making it difficult to detect for access control mechanisms and standard faithfulness checks that treat the context as an undifferentiated pool of evidence. We formalize Ghost Context, propose a taxonomy of four interference patterns, describe a mask-and-rerun detection methodology, and outline the security implications for retrieval-augmented generation and agent memory systems. We argue that reliable deployment of long-context models requires distinguishing Ghost Context from conventional hallucination and developing targeted mitigation strategies for cross-context interference.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.36227\/techrxiv.177162116.61215374\/v1","type":"posted-content","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Ghost Context: Cross-Context Hallucination in Long-Context raisonnement efficace en contexte long dans les grands mod\u00e8les de langage<\/jats:title>\n                <jats:p xml:lang=\"fr\">Les grands mod\u00e8les de langage sont de plus en plus utilis\u00e9s dans des contextes qui exigent un raisonnement sur de longs documents, des entr\u00e9es structur\u00e9es et plusieurs sources de preuves. Dans les mod\u00e8les fond\u00e9s sur les Transformers, toutefois, les contextes longs restent limit\u00e9s par trois goulots d'\u00e9tranglement \u00e9troitement li\u00e9s : le co\u00fbt quadratique de l'auto-attention lors de la phase de pr\u00e9remplissage, la croissance lin\u00e9aire du cache Key-Value (KV) pendant la g\u00e9n\u00e9ration, et la d\u00e9gradation de la qualit\u00e9 du raisonnement lorsque les \u00e9l\u00e9ments pertinents sont r\u00e9partis dans des entr\u00e9es longues ou h\u00e9t\u00e9rog\u00e8nes. Cette th\u00e8se \u00e9tudie ces limites \u00e0 travers trois principes compl\u00e9mentaires : la compression, l'amortissement et la d\u00e9composition. Premi\u00e8rement, la th\u00e8se traite le co\u00fbt m\u00e9moire de l'inf\u00e9rence en contexte long au moyen d'une compression du cache KV sensible \u00e0 la requ\u00eate. Elle introduit Finch, une m\u00e9thode sans entra\u00eenement qui utilise les propres motifs d'attention du mod\u00e8le pour conserver les entr\u00e9es du cache les plus pertinentes pour une requ\u00eate donn\u00e9e. Le m\u00eame principe guid\u00e9 par l'attention est ensuite \u00e9tendu des contextes en langage naturel aux entr\u00e9es tabulaires structur\u00e9es, montrant que la compression du cache KV peut pr\u00e9server \u00e0 la fois les informations textuelles et structurelles dans des tableaux lin\u00e9aris\u00e9s. Deuxi\u00e8mement, la th\u00e8se \u00e9tudie comment amortir le co\u00fbt de la compression lorsque plusieurs requ\u00eates sont \u00e9mises sur un m\u00eame corpus. Elle introduit CacheNotes, une m\u00e9thode de compression hors ligne sensible \u00e0 la t\u00e2che, qui construit des caches KV compress\u00e9s et r\u00e9utilisables \u00e0 partir d'un corpus et d'une description de t\u00e2che en langage naturel. Cela d\u00e9place une partie du co\u00fbt de traitement hors du temps de requ\u00eate, tout en pr\u00e9servant les informations pertinentes pour la t\u00e2che en vue d'une utilisation ult\u00e9rieure. Troisi\u00e8mement, la th\u00e8se examine le raisonnement multi-documents sans concat\u00e9ner toutes les preuves dans un seul contexte partag\u00e9. Elle introduit PCED, Parallel Context-of-Experts Decoding, qui encode les documents r\u00e9cup\u00e9r\u00e9s de mani\u00e8re ind\u00e9pendante et combine leurs contributions pendant la g\u00e9n\u00e9ration au moyen d'un d\u00e9codage contrastif tenant compte de la r\u00e9cup\u00e9ration. Cette formulation d\u00e9compos\u00e9e r\u00e9duit les interf\u00e9rences entre documents et am\u00e9liore l'efficacit\u00e9 de l'agr\u00e9gation des preuves. Ensemble, ces contributions montrent que le raisonnement en contexte long peut \u00eatre rendu plus efficace non seulement en \u00e9tendant les fen\u00eatres de contexte, mais aussi en s\u00e9lectionnant, en r\u00e9utilisant et en combinant de mani\u00e8re modulaire les repr\u00e9sentations contextuelles.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.70675\/35354b1fzad3bz42edzb474z6cf1067d0599","type":"dissertation","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Compress, Amortize, Decompose : Efficient Long-Context Reasoning in Large Language Models"],"author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0009-0009-5561-5479","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Giulio","family":"Corallo","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"id":[{"id":"https:\/\/ror.org\/02en5vm52","id-type":"ROR","asserted-by":"publisher"}],"name":"Sorbonne universit\u00e9"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[null]]},"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.70675\/35354b1fzad3bz42edzb474z6cf1067d0599"},{"abstract":"<jats:p>The rapid increase in unstructured data across various fields has made multi-document comprehension and summarization a critical task. Traditional approaches often fail to capture relevant context, maintain logical consistency, and extract essential information from lengthy documents. This paper explores the use of Long-context Large Language Models (LLMs) for multi-document summarization, demonstrating their exceptional capacity to grasp extensive connections, provide cohesive summaries, and adapt to various industry domains and integration with enterprise applications\/systems. The paper discusses the workflow of multi-document summarization for effectively deploying long-context LLMs, supported by case studies in legal applications, enterprise functions such as HR, finance, and sourcing, as well as in the medical and news domains. These case studies show notable enhancements in both efficiency and accuracy. Technical obstacles, such as dataset diversity, model scalability, and ethical considerations like bias mitigation and factual accuracy, are carefully analyzed. Prospective research avenues are suggested to augment the functionalities and applications of long-context LLMs, establishing them as pivotal tools for transforming information processing across
